name: @olai/tests
//scripts: Bun hosts the runner, and `test` NAMES cucumber's entry file so that it does. Bun executes `.ts` natively, so there is no tsx, no ts-node and no build step between a step definition and the browser driving it — but only while bun is the thing reading those files, and a bin name does not guarantee that. `cucumber-js` is a shebang file (`#!/usr/bin/env node`), and `bun run <script>` EXECUTES a package script's argv rather than interpreting it, so the shebang is resolved against PATH. Bun does put a `node`-to-bun shim on that PATH — but ONLY when no real node is there (`/tmp/bun-node-*` appears in the child's PATH exactly when `command -v node` finds nothing else). That is the trap: the arrangement was verified with node removed from PATH entirely, which is the one condition where the fallback applies. A developer with node installed gets the real one — including inside `nix develop .#e2e`, which APPENDS the host's PATH rather than replacing it — and the whole suite dies before its first scenario with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING, node refusing the raw-TypeScript @kolu/* sources. Handing the .js file to bun leaves no shebang to lose: bun is the interpreter on any host, in or out of the shell. Keep it a path, never a bin name — runner.test.ts pins that. The path is stable because the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) gives every package its own direct dependencies.
//dependencies: @olai/web for the NAMES it owns and nothing else: the `data-testid` record (support/world.ts), the day arithmetic in clock.ts, and the theme table's attribute, storage key and default. @olai/fonts is the same arrangement one package over — the TYPEFACE table's attribute, storage key and default, imported from the package that owns them rather than from the client that draws them. Each is a contract between two packages that never otherwise meet, and the way that kind of contract breaks is silent — a rename compiles on both sides and shows up as a thirty-second timeout. Importing makes it a type error instead. @olai/format is here for two NAMES on the same terms: `MARKS`, the three fields a record may carry, so the disk assertion that a node is UNMARKED is written against the format's own list rather than three field names this suite would spell alone and quietly stop covering the day a fourth arrived — and `FILE_KINDS`, the table saying which files a served directory is made of, so the sweeps in kinds.test.ts hunt the suffixes the format actually claims rather than a list of them kept here. @olai/surface is the same again for the two halves of what a `.html` preview IS on the wire: `mediaHref`, the address a preview frame is pointed at, and `sealPolicy`, the exact content policy the server answers it with — so the scenario that says a preview is sealed reads the policy the server writes rather than a copy of it that could go on passing after the real one was widened. No BEHAVIOUR is imported from any of them: these tests drive the client through a browser, not through its modules.
//devDependencies: @olai/log is here for its `./testlib` DECODER only: the readiness signal this suite waits on is a line on the server's stdout, and that line's format belongs to @olai/log — so the thing that reads it back is @olai/log's too, rather than a regex this suite would maintain alone and silently stop matching the day a value needed quoting. playwright is pinned to 1.61.1 — the version of `pkgs.playwright-driver` in the pinned nixpkgs. The npm package ships only the driver's JS; the browsers come from the Nix store via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, and the driver refuses a browser build it was not compiled against. A minor-version drift here (kolu's 1.59.0, say) does not fail at install time — it fails at `chromium.launch()` with "Executable doesn't exist", pointing at a path inside the store that is real but wrong. Bump this only together with the nixpkgs pin, never on its own.
